title: Teams bridge: relay kith chats to/from Microsoft Teams
description:
A standalone bridge process that relays messages bidirectionally between kith and Microsoft Teams. Runs on any host with tailnet access to the user's kithd.

Architecture:
- Bridge holds Azure AD app registration credentials (app ID + secret or certificate) and kithd JMAP credentials
- Teams → kith: receive Teams messages via Bot Framework webhook or Graph API change notifications (webhooks require public URL; polling the Graph API is an alternative for no-ingress deployments)
- kith → Teams: subscribe to kithd EventSource; post to Teams channel via Graph API sendChatMessage
- Each bridged Teams channel/chat maps to a kith chat ID

Scope:
- Azure AD app registration (documented setup steps; not automated)
- Graph API: POST /teams/{id}/channels/{id}/messages, GET /chats/{id}/messages
- Change notifications via Graph webhooks OR fallback polling (every 30s) for no-public-URL deployments
- Message deduplication; graceful reconnect
- Attachment bridging: download from Teams (Graph driveItem download URL), upload to kithd blob endpoint
- Identity: Teams messages attributed to synthetic kith contact; kith messages posted as bot with sender prefix
- Target: Rust or Go binary; systemd service unit included

Key decisions for research phase:
- Webhook vs polling for Teams→kith direction (polling avoids public URL requirement, fits tailnet model)
- Personal app (single-tenant AAD) vs multi-tenant — single-tenant preferred (user controls their own AAD app)
- Teams personal chats vs channel posts vs both
